title: Separate Place vs Our World
use_cases: Use when categorizing a manuscript based on geographical setting
Implement when distinguishing between High Fantasy and Magical Realism
Configure when establishing narrative rules for a fictional world
Use when evaluating the role of escapism versus social commentary in a text
content:
This is the biggest clue. Ask yourself: Where does this story happen?

If the answer is “Middle-earth,” “Narnia,” “Hogwarts,” or any place with its own map at the front of the book, it is fantasy. Fantasy authors work hard at fantasy world-building vs realism. They want you to escape to a new place. This new place has its own rules.

If the answer is “a small town in Colombia,” “a family’s kitchen in Mexico,” or “modern-day Tokyo,” it is probably magical realism. The setting is our real, normal world. The author wants you to look at our world in a new, strange way. The story explores realism in fantasy stories by grounding the magic in a real place.
